evidence:
Authored for this product. The brief opens with a HireOps-specific problem that no sibling states: 'Sometimes both requisitions are fully committed: the exchange is affordable as a whole, but neither move can happen first' (task/instruction.md, paragraph 1), then stale previews 'even if a budget was changed and later restored to the same balance' and replay of 'the original receipt, including after later revisions, rescissions or a server restart' (paragraph 2). The rules file is product-specific end to end: equity intrinsic value = units x max(0, fair value - strike), annualised over 4 years (hireops_rules.md section 2); run-rate versus approval-band basis with the signing bonus weighed at half (section 2); two different vesting schedules, 40%+5%/month to 24 months and 20%+4%/month to 32 months (section 6); referral halves against a 6-month cliff read at the stored reference moment (section 7); netted two-to-four-member change sets with operation keys and made-then-reversed staleness (section 11); the live change desk (section 12). task.toml is filled in for this product: name 'turing/hireops-recruiting-operations', arena_slice 'recruiting-hiring-operations', provenance 'Adapted from the supplied HireOps task ...', keywords recruiting/compensation/ledger; none of the template's CHANGE_ME placeholders remain.

No sibling residue. A case-insensitive grep of the whole frozen task for pellmoor, expenseflow, drawbill, docketlight, torquebay, bazaarbridge, oriel, medledger, colderwater, northline, northstar, pixeldeck, snake, vacancy, lorem and TODO returned zero hits. All 164 criterion names (1 render, 1 constraints, 152 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual) carry the hro_ prefix and name HireOps concepts (hro_intrinsic, hro_basis, hro_claw, hro_referral_clock, hro_change_aba, hro_change_net_budget, hro_live_stale_mark, hro_whatif_roles).

Not a nouns-swapped clone. I measured 8-word shingle overlap between HireOps (instruction.md + hireops_rules.md, 6563 shingles; functional judge.toml, 11099 shingles) and every .md and judge.toml under projects/. The largest overlap on the brief side is expenseflow_rules.md at 121 shingles (about 1.8%), confined to 12 lines of shared house preamble in hireops_rules.md: 'relocated, topic by topic, from our own working notes' (lines 4-5), session identity (line 26), the stored reference moment (line 59), integer storage and round-half-up (lines 71, 79-80), and the 401/403 discipline (lines 359-371). ExpenseFlow's mechanics are FX conversion, policy caps, per-diem proration, reclaimable tax and a cost-center split with a plug; none of them appears in HireOps, and HireOps's equity, vesting, referral, coordinated-change and live-desk rules do not appear in ExpenseFlow. On the criteria side the maximum overlap is 55 shingles, identical for the template, Ridgeline and Colderwater functional judge.toml files, so it is template judge scaffolding, not task-specific criteria; it is 18 for the legacy-layout siblings including Pellmoor.

Same-domain sibling checked. projects/pellmoor-job-pipeline is also hiring. Its flows are stage gating ('nobody jumps a stage'), panels, scores, notes, fresh assessments, vacancy capacity and a d3 funnel on a TypeScript/esbuild stack. HireOps has none of those and is a compensation offer and budget ledger. The two touch only at a generic level (atomic multi-offer action; capacity that competing offers cannot overbook versus requisition headroom), with different entities, rules and criteria.

Limits of this review. I found no standalone suite domain-plan document in the workspace (grep for 'domain plan', 'arena_slice' and 'recruiting' across NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md, TASK_AUTHORING_WORKFLOW.md, qc/README.md, qc/CURRENT.md and WebDev_guide.md returned nothing), so 'fits the suite's domain plan' was judged the way quality-checks.md:213 prescribes, by comparing sibling task names and concepts, plus the declared arena_slice. If a plan exists outside this workspace that forbids two hiring-domain tasks, the Pellmoor adjacency should be rechecked against it. Sibling briefs were read only in their opening sections; the full-text comparison is the shingle measurement. I did not recompute the input SHA256; the value preserved here matches manifest.json and raw-evidence-index.json. No runtime evidence bears on this row.

Adversarial checks from the assignment. A broken app that could pass, or a conforming alternative that could fail, is not a meaningful probe for this row, which judges authorship of the task text and not app behaviour. The nearest equivalent is a clone that would pass a name-only check; the shingle measurement and concept comparison above are aimed at that case.
